reference: Page, Aviation Engines (1917), chapters VIII-XII (P1); British Air Board, The Care of the 100 hp Monosoupape Engine (1917) and Technical Notes (1918); see cad-studies/gnome-monosoupape-1913/research.md.
scope: Source-led teaching reconstruction of the 100 hp Gnome Monosoupape Type B-2 nine-cylinder rotary (1913), drawn from Page's Aviation Engines (1917) and the British Air Board handbook; it is not a museum object, not a manufacturing drawing and not a running model. Dimensions the sources do not give are estimates (the master and auxiliary rod lengths, the knuckle radius, wall thicknesses). The operating motion is illustrative: the fixed crankshaft with the case, cylinders and propeller turning about it, the master rod with eight auxiliary rods, the 1-3-5-7-9-2-4-6-8 firing order, the 85 to 475 degree single-valve window with 11.5 mm lift and the half-speed cam sleeve follow the sources. The lift curve inside that window, the rocker and pushrod geometry, the planet-pinion spin and the cam lobes are teaching choices; the lobes are schematic and do not drive the tappets. Valve timing is keyed to the nominal 40 degree cylinder spacing, while the articulated rods shift each piston's true top dead centre by up to 5 degrees, as on the real engine. The magneto, the pump and the spark are not animated.

stages.label: Cylinder 1 at top dead centre, firing
stages.note: Cylinder 1 is at the top of its compression stroke and fires. The crankshaft and its crankpin never move: the case, the nine cylinders and the propeller turn about them, and each piston's rod pulls it toward the fixed crankpin as its cylinder swings round.

stages.label: Half a case turn
stages.note: The case has turned 180 degrees. Cylinders fire every 80 degrees in the order 1-3-5-7-9-2-4-6-8, so cylinders 3 and 5 have fired since cylinder 1. The single overhead valve of cylinder 1 opened at 85 degrees, early in the stroke, to let the exhaust out.

stages.label: One case turn
stages.note: Cylinder 1 is back at the top with its valve still open: on the Monosoupape the one valve stays open into the next stroke and draws in fresh air. The cam sleeve has turned half as far as the case.

stages.label: Three half-turns
stages.note: Cylinder 1's valve closed at 115 degrees past the top; the piston kept going down and made a vacuum, then uncovered the skirt ports near the bottom so rich mixture rushed in from the crankcase. That is why the engine needs only one valve.

stages.label: Two case turns: one four-stroke cycle
stages.note: Every cylinder has fired once. The lift curve, the rocker and pushrod geometry and the cam lobes here are teaching choices; the window, the lift and the firing order follow the sources.

stages.label: Assembled
stages.note: The engine as modelled: every part in its assembled position, cylinder 1 at the top and every valve closed.

stages.label: Nose, cam drive and accessories
stages.note: At the front the propeller hub, the nose cover, the cam gear case with its tappets, the nine-cam sleeve and the epicyclic planet gears move forward along the shaft; at the rear the distributor ring, the magneto drive and the fuselage bearer plates move back. The spark plugs leave the cylinders.

stages.label: Valve gear
stages.note: Each cylinder's overhead valve train moves out along its own axis: the rocker and its pillar, the pushrod, the valve with its spring and guide cage.

stages.label: Cylinders, pistons and crankcase
stages.note: The nine cylinders with their clamps and port belts move out along their axes, the pistons part from the auxiliary rods, and the two crankcase bowls and the tie bolts separate along the shaft. The fixed crankshaft with the master rod and the eight auxiliary rods stays as the reference.

viewpoint: Axes: the crankshaft runs along x with the propeller at the front (-x) and the fuselage at the rear (+x), z is up and cylinder 1 points up at the assembled pose. The crankpin is fixed at +z; the case turns clockwise seen from the cockpit (from +x looking forward).
